title: Notion Review (2026)
intro: Notion is evaluated here as a docs-first workspace with light project tracking — Notion is a docs-first knowledge and database workspace used for wikis, specs and lightweight project tracking. Free for personal use; Plus ~$10/user/mo annual; Business ~$20 with Notion AI bundled in common 2026 packaging; Enterprise custom. Strong for knowledge work — lighter than dedicated Work OS peers for portfolio PM. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Notion when documentation and flexible databases are the primary job, with light project tracking layered on — not as a pure Work OS substitute.
verdict: Choose Notion when documentation and flexible databases are the primary job, with light project tracking layered on — not as a pure Work OS substitute. Compare Asana/ClickUp/monday for dedicated Work OS execution, Airtable for heavier DB apps, and Jira for engineering delivery. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Approachable for knowledge workers; databases can get complex but onboarding is friendlier than Jira.
Light project tracking via databases/boards — not a dedicated Work OS planning depth peer.
Automations exist but thinner than ClickUp/Asana/monday.
Docs, comments and shared workspaces are Notion’s centre of gravity — top collaboration score.
Solid connector set; not as deep as monday/Jira ecosystems.
Limited native PM dashboards vs Work OS peers — held at 5.
Works for startups to mid-market knowledge orgs; enterprise governance on higher tiers.
Plus $10 is fair for docs+DB; Business AI bundle drives TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
Notion AI is a major 2026 buying reason on Business — strong for writing/Q&A, not sprint AI.

bestFor: Buyers who want Notion AI writing/search
cons: Can become a messy wiki without standards
Not a Work OS peer on undifferentiated ranks
limitations: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management
Reporting/dashboards thinner than dedicated PM tools
pricingSummary: Free personal; Plus $10, Business ~$20 annual (AI often bundled on Business); Enterprise custom. Confirm live.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Notion when documentation and flexible databases are the primary job, with light project tracking layered on — not as a pure Work OS substitute.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Compare Asana/ClickUp/monday for dedicated Work OS execution, Airtable for heavier DB apps, and Jira for engineering delivery.

faq.question: Is Notion a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: No. Notion is an adjacent desktop workspace organizer. It wraps web apps into desktop shells — it is not a project tracker or work OS.

faq.question: How is Notion priced?
faq.answer: Free personal; Plus $10, Business ~$20 annual (AI often bundled on Business); Enterprise custom. Confirm live.

faq.question: Does Notion have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Notion?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
